comparisons.peer_topic: Payment Default Rates for Recent Consumer Real Estate TDRs
comparisons.peer_summary: The bank discloses the carrying value of consumer real estate loans that entered payment default during 2022 which had been modified in a TDR within the 12 months preceding the default; default is recognized after missing three monthly payments since modification, excluding loans with unpaid trial modification offers.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose the carrying value of consumer loans modified as TDRs that subsequently entered payment default within 12 months of modification. JPM defines this as loans that defaulted within one year, measuring the balance at the end of the default period. BAC similarly tracks consumer real estate loans defaulting within the 12 months preceding the reporting date, but provides a specific operational definition of default (missing three monthly payments) and explicitly excludes loans with unpaid trial modification offers from the default count, whereas JPM's definition is broader regarding the timing of the default event relative to modification.

sentences.text: (a)Represents loans permanently modified in TDRs that experienced a payment default in the periods presented, and for which the payment default occurred within one year of the modification.
The dollar amounts presented represent the balance of such loans at the end of the reporting period in which such loans defaulted.
The table below presents the carrying value of consumer real estate loans that entered into payment default during 2022 that were modified in a TDR during the 12 months preceding payment default.
A payment default for consumer real estate TDRs is recognized when a borrower has missed three monthly payments (not necessarily consecutively) since modification.

comparisons.peer_summary: No modified corporate loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty defaulted during the year ended December 31, 2024. Default is defined as 60 days past due, except for classifiably managed commercial banking loans, where default is defined as 90 days past due. For non-collateral dependent modified corporate loans, expected default rates are considered in the individually assessed allowance for credit losses.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the status of modified loans experiencing financial difficulty regarding subsequent defaults. JPM defines 'TDR payment defaults' specifically for the consumer loan portfolio, tracking balances of loans that defaulted within one year of modification. Citi, in contrast, reports on modified corporate loans, stating that none defaulted during the year ended December 31, 2024, and provides a distinct definition of default for these commercial loans (60 or 90 days past due) compared to JPM's 12-month window focus.

comparisons.peer_topic: Past Due Loans Modified Prior to Default
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, there were two commercial real estate loans held for investment with a total amortized cost of $56 million that defaulted during the year and had been modified in the 12-month period prior to default, whereas there were no such loans in 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Morgan Stanley disclose instances where loans modified as TDRs defaulted shortly after modification. JPM reports the aggregate dollar balance of such consumer loans that defaulted within one year of modification. Morgan Stanley reports specific quantities and amortized cost ($56 million in 2024 for commercial real estate loans) of loans that defaulted during the year having been modified in the preceding 12-month period, noting that this was a new occurrence compared to 2023.
